verified.exploit_entry_point: Member-side compact deserialization: InternalSerializationService.toObject(Data) -> CompactStreamSerializer.read -> getOrCreateRegistration(schema.getTypeName()) -> ReflectiveCompactSerializer.read. The same path serves every client value the member deserializes (map values, operation arguments). Tests build the same service the member builds (DefaultSerializationServiceBuilder) and write the attacker value as a GenericRecord, with the schema in the schema service and (one case) carried in the binary.

traps.lever_mechanism: M8 shape a plausible check mishandles: a verification that already exists but runs only after the object has been constructed, so the fix must place eligibility before allocation

traps.lever_mechanism: M8 shape a plausible check mishandles: the eligibility decision for the element is right, but the containing value cannot be delivered at that position, so the fallback must cover the position rather than only the class it names

wrong_fix_catalogue.crash_as_refusal: n/a: the security tests require a generic-record result (or, where a nested position cannot hold one, a clean failure) and never accept a crash; a crash fails the top-level tests
wrong_fix_catalogue.wrong_resource: n/a: there is no authorisation decision over a resource; the property is about the class a wire type name denotes
wrong_fix_catalogue.one_role_or_direction: n/a: the read path has no roles, peers or directions; every client value follows the same rule
wrong_fix_catalogue.reads_only: n/a: the flaw is the member's deserialization of client data; there is no write-side authority the tests depend on
wrong_fix_catalogue.malformed_identity: n/a: no identity, name or credential is parsed on the protected path
wrong_fix_catalogue.missing_authority: n/a: eligibility is decided from the class and the deployment's own configuration, not from an authority that could return nothing and fail open

lever_audit.note: The how-type levers require the deserialization mechanism to be understood (eligibility before allocation, separate nested/record/array read paths, a platform decision by module rather than package name, containing-value fallback when a nested value cannot be delivered, a default restriction list, and real shipped routes the published fix left open). 2026-10-22 hardening added the module-based platform route and the eligible-component array fallback; both were real code paths the previous oracle left open and the instruction already covered.
